title: WASAPI microphone capture returns silent audio when SteelSeries Sonar is running
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.6.2.stable (71f334935), 4.0.4.stable


### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable (71f334935) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.91 GiB memory

### Issue description


I ran into a reproducible microphone recording issue with the official [mic_record demo](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/audio/mic_record) on Windows. When [SteelSeries Sonar](https://steelseries.com/gg/sonar#sonar) is running, Godot records audio with the correct byte length, but the entire buffer contains only zeroes.

## Environment

- Godot: 4.6 stable, official build
- OS: Windows 11 24H2 / 25H2
- Audio driver: WASAPI
- Reproduction project: official [`mic_record` demo](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/audio/mic_record)
- Related software: [SteelSeries GG / SteelSeries Sonar](https://steelseries.com/gg/sonar#sonar)

## Actual Behavior

The `AudioStreamWAV` produced by the `mic_record` demo has the expected byte length for the recording duration, but the buffer is entirely filled with `0` values. Playback is silent, and the saved `.wav` file is also silent.

The physical microphone itself works correctly in other applications, including Discord, OBS, the Windows sound settings input meter, and several games or other microphone-using applications. I have been using Sonar for 2-3 years, and this is the first time I have encountered this kind of issue.

## Expected Behavior

Godot should record real microphone samples from the selected input device instead of receiving an all-zero buffer.

## Reproduction

I was able to narrow this down using two machines.

### Machine A

Windows 11 25H2, SteelSeries Sonar already installed.

1. Run the official `mic_record` demo.
2. Record audio.
3. The result is silent. The byte length is correct, but the buffer is all zeroes.
4. Disable Sonar from the SteelSeries interface.
5. Set the Windows default input device to the physical microphone.
6. Record again in Godot. Recording works normally, without restarting Godot.

### Machine B

Windows 11 24H2, SteelSeries Sonar had never been installed before.

1. Run the official `mic_record` demo.
2. Recording works normally. This was the baseline.
3. Install SteelSeries GG / Sonar using the official installer. No other system changes were made.
4. Run the `mic_record` demo again.
5. Recording becomes silent, with the same symptoms as Machine A: correct byte length, but an all-zero buffer.

On Machine B, the behavior changed from working to silent immediately after installing Sonar, which strongly suggests that Sonar is the trigger.

## Important Observation

At first I thought this was simply caused by Sonar setting its virtual microphone as the Windows default input device. However, the behavior seems to be deeper than just default device selection:

1. Sonar running, Windows default input set to Sonar virtual microphone: Godot records silence.
2. Sonar running, Windows default input explicitly set to the physical microphone: Godot still records silence.
3. Sonar disabled, Windows default input set to the physical microphone: Godot records normally, without restarting Godot.

So, bypassing the Sonar virtual device in Windows input settings is not enough. Sonar has to be actually disabled before Godot's WASAPI capture receives real samples.

At the same time, while Sonar is still running, other applications such as Discord, OBS, Windows sound settings, and games can still record from the same physical microphone correctly. This makes me suspect that the issue may be related to the specific WASAPI capture path used by Godot, rather than a general Windows input routing problem.

## Things I Tried

- Verified that Windows microphone privacy settings allow desktop apps to access the microphone.
- Explicitly set `AudioServer.input_device` in `_ready()` to the physical microphone device name.
- Changed the Windows default input device to the physical microphone while Sonar was still running, making sure Godot was not supposed to use the Sonar virtual microphone.

## Additional Notes

I am not familiar enough with Godot's WASAPI backend to know whether its capture path differs from Discord, OBS, or games in terms of endpoint selection, capture mode, format negotiation, or buffer handling. From the outside, it looks like SteelSeries Sonar may interfere with the specific WASAPI capture path Godot uses, causing Godot to receive buffers with the correct length but with all samples set to zero.

If anyone familiar with the WASAPI driver can suggest what information would be useful, I would be happy to provide logs, device lists, sample `.wav` files, or run additional tests.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install [SteelSeries GG](https://steelseries.com/gg/sonar#sonar) using the official installer. 
2. Enable Sonar in SteelSeries GG .
3. Run the `mic_record` demo.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mic_record.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27811961/mic_record.zip)
or
https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/audio/mic_record
